subject: great snipe
title: A Plump Wading Bird Flew 4,225 Miles Nonstop in 3.5 Days

scenes.text: The fastest long-distance flier isn't a falcon. It's chubby.
Meet the great snipe, a plump little wading bird that nests in Sweden.
Scientists tagged ten males. One flew four thousand two hundred miles to central Africa without landing.
Three and a half days, at up to sixty miles an hour, with little help from wind.
How? Before leaving, they almost double their body weight, mostly fuel they burn on the way.
So that chubby look isn't laziness. It's a full fuel tank.

description:
Great snipes tracked from Sweden flew up to 4,225 miles to central Africa without stopping, in about three and a half days.
They reach ground speeds of up to 60 mph with little tailwind help, after almost doubling their body weight before the trip. The study was published in Biology Letters.
Could you stay awake for three and a half days?
first_comment: Most migrating songbirds stop to refuel every few hundred miles. Great snipes fly straight over Europe and the Sahara. Which bird would you bet on in a race?
